title: Bootstrap: how sure is the tree?
summary: Predict which grouping the data supports least, then resample and see.

prompts.concept: These eight sequences share a true tree, but the alignment is deliberately short. Build the NJ tree, then step to the end to ask: how sure are we that each grouping is real?
prompts.math: A short internal branch leaves few sites where its grouping differs from the rest — exactly the sites a resample can miss.

prompts.concept: Before you run, make a prediction: which internal branch of the inferred tree will the data support least? Click that branch — terminal branches don't count — then run the bootstrap.
prompts.math: Each replicate resamples the 300 columns with replacement and rebuilds the tree; a grouping's support is the share of successful replicate trees that contain it.
prompts.reveal: The weakest grouping is the one on the true tree's shortest internal branch. At 300 columns, only a handful of sites carry evidence for it, so many resampled datasets rebuild a different grouping there.

prompts.concept: Support is an estimate too. Change the bootstrap Seed and run again: the numbers shift by a few points, because each run draws different resamples. With 1,000 replicates instead of 100, they settle down. So don't read much into small differences like 52 versus 57.
Now try more data. Raise Length to 3,000 — ten times as many columns — and run again. Watch what happens to that grouping's support.
prompts.math: Signal scales with sites: the same tree under 10× the columns puts ~10× the expected substitutions on every branch, short ones included.

prompts.concept: Read the numbers carefully. When a grouping shows 87, it means 87 of 100 resampled datasets rebuilt it, not that it has an 87% chance of being true. Support measures how consistently the data points to a grouping. Low support means this dataset says little about that grouping, not that the grouping is wrong: here the weak grouping was real, and a longer alignment raised its support. Small differences between seeds or runs are noise; don't overinterpret them.
